_comment: Generated by scripts/build_visual_catalog.py - do not edit by hand. Authored prose lives in content.json; everything else here is derived from manifest.csv, the .pbiviz packages when present, visual-allowlist.json, icons.lock.json and the gallery PBIR.

generatedFrom.roles: each .pbiviz capabilities.dataRoles, captured once so a clone without packages still has them

visuals.name: Accessible table
visuals.useWhen: A table variant optimised for assistive technology, where screen-reader output is the governing requirement.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. It appears in the CLI catalog but its Desktop availability is unverified, so treat it as a finding rather than an option.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Desktop availability unverified.

visuals.name: Button
visuals.useWhen: Give the reader an explicit, visible control to navigate, reset filters or trigger an action.
visuals.notFor: Actions that should happen without being asked for. Note that PBIR cannot encode button navigation at all - the report-author CLI exposes no metadata for it, so wire the action in Desktop.

visuals.name: Button slicer
visuals.useWhen: A filter as buttons, when the available values are few enough to show all at once as a deliberate choice.
visuals.notFor: High-cardinality fields. Button slicers do not scroll, so a long value list will not fit.

visuals.name: Smart narrative
visuals.exclusionReason: Smart narrative did not render in Desktop; the sample uses `narrative` instead.
visuals.useWhen: A written summary that selects its own insight from the bound data.
visuals.notFor: PBIR authoring - it did not render in Desktop when this gallery was verified. Use narrative, which summarises a page or a visual placed beside it.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type, but the same shape as narrative. Drawn identically.

visuals.name: Animated number
visuals.useWhen: A number that animates as it changes.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. Catalogued, Desktop availability unverified.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Desktop availability unverified.

visuals.name: Area chart
visuals.useWhen: Emphasise the magnitude of change in a total over time, where the shape of the curve is itself the message.
visuals.notFor: More than two or three series, which occlude each other. Use stackedAreaChart for cumulative composition, or lineChart when comparing values precisely.

visuals.name: Azure Maps
visuals.exclusionReason: Requires a provisioned Azure Maps account; not authorable in a self-contained sample.
visuals.useWhen: Bing-backed maps with data-driven shapes and layers, where the tenant has an Azure Maps account provisioned.
visuals.notFor: A self-contained report. The account requirement makes it unauthorable in this sample, and it is an external dependency rather than a visual choice - use map or shapeMap.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Shares the map glyph; the reason it cannot be authored here is a missing Azure Maps account, not its appearance.

visuals.name: Bar chart
visuals.useWhen: The same comparison as a column chart, but when category labels are long text that would otherwise have to rotate.
visuals.notFor: A time axis. Readers scan a sequence most naturally left to right, so use columnChart for periods.

visuals.name: Basic shape
visuals.useWhen: The primitive rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse or line that shape is built from.
visuals.notFor: Anything data-driven.

visuals.name: Bookmark navigator
visuals.useWhen: Let the reader step through saved report states in sequence.
visuals.notFor: Page navigation. Use pageNavigator for pages, bookmarkNavigator for bookmark states - they are different things.

visuals.name: Card (legacy)
visuals.useWhen: Nothing. Present only so the gallery can explain why it is absent.
visuals.notFor: Any new work. Use cardVisual, which supports multiple values, images and reference labels in one visual.

thumbnail.reason: Legacy. Shares the cardVisual glyph; use cardVisual instead.

visuals.name: Card
visuals.useWhen: Make one number the most important thing on the page.
visuals.notFor: Comparing several measures. Past two or three side by side, cards stop being scannable; use a small table or the kpi visual.

visuals.name: Clustered bar chart
visuals.useWhen: Compare a measure across categories with long labels, split by a second dimension.
visuals.notFor: The same cases as barChart. Nothing distinguishes the clustered form visually except the extra series, so prefer a column chart and a legend unless the labels force horizontal bars.

thumbnail.reason: No distinct glyph exists for the clustered variant; the bar form is the same chart with a second field split into series. Use the combo schematic to see that difference.

visuals.name: Clustered column chart
visuals.useWhen: Compare a measure across categories and split it by a second, low-cardinality dimension such as channel or region.
visuals.notFor: A split dimension with many levels; the bars stop being readable. Use lineChart instead when both dimensions are ordered in time.

visuals.name: Column chart
visuals.useWhen: Compare a measure across a small number of discrete categories, most often a period on the X axis.
visuals.notFor: Long category names, or more than roughly a dozen categories. Use barChart when labels need room, and pivotTable when the reader needs exact values rather than a shape.

visuals.name: Data query
visuals.useWhen: A visual that lets the reader author and run a query against the model.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. Catalogued, Desktop availability unverified, and it also raises a governance question about ad hoc query access in a report.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Desktop availability unverified.

visuals.name: Decomposition tree
visuals.useWhen: Let a reader break a total down along whichever dimension they choose, to find what is driving it.
visuals.notFor: A guided explanation. It is exploratory by design and gives the reader full control over the path taken.

visuals.name: Donut chart
visuals.useWhen: Part-to-whole where the open centre can carry a total, a label or an icon.
visuals.notFor: The same cases as pieChart. The hole adds a place for a number but does not improve value comparison.

visuals.name: Filled map
visuals.useWhen: Shade geographic regions by a measure where you have region or country codes.
visuals.notFor: Point-level detail. Use map when the position of individual places is the message.

visuals.name: Filter slicer
visuals.useWhen: A slicer variant in the catalog.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. Catalogued, Desktop availability unverified. Use slicer.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Shares the button-slicer glyph; its Desktop availability is unverified rather than its appearance.

visuals.name: Funnel
visuals.useWhen: Show sequential stages of a process with drop-off between them, such as a sales pipeline or a conversion chain.
visuals.notFor: Stages that are not strictly ordered, or whose widths are not proportional to counts - the taper becomes decorative.

visuals.name: Gauge
visuals.useWhen: Show the health of a single measure against a goal on a radial scale.
visuals.notFor: Comparing several measures. Radial area is very hard to compare across gauges; use cardVisual or kpi for a set.

visuals.name: Heat map
visuals.useWhen: A matrix coloured by value.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. Catalogued, Desktop availability unverified, and note this is a distinct visual type from applying conditional formatting to tableEx - do not assume the two are interchangeable.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Desktop availability unverified; Power BI's heatMap catalog entry is distinct from conditional formatting on any other visual.

visuals.name: 100% stacked area chart
visuals.useWhen: Show how the mix of components shifts over time when the absolute total is not the point.
visuals.notFor: Any question about volume. Normalising removes the height cue, so this visual cannot answer 'did it grow?' - put a lineChart of the total beside it.

thumbnail.reason: 100% stacking normalises every column to the same height, which is the one thing the chart-area outline cannot convey. Drawn as a normalised stack.

visuals.name: 100% stacked bar chart
visuals.useWhen: Compare proportional composition across categories whose labels are long.
visuals.notFor: As for the column variant: not for volume, and not for trend.

thumbnail.reason: Same reason as the column variant. Drawn as a normalised stack.

visuals.name: 100% stacked column chart
visuals.useWhen: Compare proportional composition between categories, where every column sums to the same height.
visuals.notFor: Volume comparison and trend detection. The normalisation hides which periods were larger and flattens the shape into a repeating pattern.

thumbnail.reason: Same reason as the area variant: normalisation removes the height cue the column glyph relies on. Drawn as a normalised stack.

visuals.name: Image
visuals.useWhen: Place a static or data-driven image, such as a logo, or a photo bound to a category.
visuals.notFor: Charts. It carries no data roles and shows no data.

visuals.name: Key influencers
visuals.useWhen: Show which factors are contributing to or detracting from a selected measure.
visuals.notFor: Proving causation, and small datasets where the ranking is unstable run to run.

thumbnail.reason: Key influencers is a list of drivers each labelled increasing or decreasing, which no glyph encodes. Drawn as signed driver rows.

visuals.name: KPI
visuals.useWhen: Pair a current value with a target and a status indicator, for progress toward a goal.
visuals.notFor: Trend analysis. A KPI shows status, not history; put a sparkline or a lineChart beside it if the reader needs direction.

thumbnail.reason: A KPI is a value plus a status indicator plus a target, which reads as a single arrow. Drawn as a value tile with a state and a goal.

visuals.name: Line chart
visuals.useWhen: Show how a measure moves over time, or along any continuous ordered axis.
visuals.notFor: Unrelated categories. Connecting the points asserts a relationship that is not there; use columnChart for a plain comparison.

visuals.name: Combo chart, clustered column and line
visuals.useWhen: Compare two measures on different scales in one plot, typically volume as columns against margin, growth or a rolling average as a line.
visuals.notFor: Two measures on a comparable scale. A single lineChart or columnChart is easier to read than a dual axis, and dual axes invite false visual correlation.

thumbnail.reason: A combo is two marks on two axes at once, which no single glyph represents. Drawn as columns with an overlaid line.

visuals.name: Combo chart, stacked column and line
visuals.useWhen: Compare a measure shown as a stacked column composition against a second measure as a line.
visuals.notFor: As for the clustered combo: prefer one axis when the scales allow it.

thumbnail.reason: As above, with a stacked column mark instead of a clustered one.

visuals.name: List slicer
visuals.useWhen: A filter as a scrollable multi-select list, when a dropdown would hide the available options.
visuals.notFor: A field with only a few values, where a dropdown is clearer and takes less space. Preview feature.

visuals.name: Map
visuals.useWhen: Plot points by latitude and longitude to show geographic distribution.
visuals.notFor: Country or region totals, which aggregate better in filledMap or shapeMap.

visuals.name: Matrix (legacy)
visuals.useWhen: Nothing. Present only so the gallery can explain why it is absent.
visuals.notFor: Any new work. Use pivotTable.

thumbnail.reason: Legacy. Use pivotTable.

visuals.name: Multi-row card (legacy)
visuals.exclusionReason: Legacy. Use cardVisual with several values in Data.
visuals.useWhen: Nothing. Present only so the gallery can explain why it is absent.
visuals.notFor: Any new work. Use cardVisual with several values in Data.

thumbnail.reason: Legacy. Use cardVisual with several values in Data.

visuals.name: Narrative
visuals.useWhen: Add a written summary of a page or an adjacent visual, stating the takeaway in words next to the evidence.
visuals.notFor: Insight it cannot support. It summarises whatever is bound to it and does not compute a new finding; bind it to the visual it is meant to describe.

thumbnail.reason: Narrative output is prose with a headline and insight lines. Drawn as a narrative card.

visuals.name: Page navigator
visuals.useWhen: Let the reader move between pages without a hand-built tab or bookmark list.
visuals.notFor: A curated navigation experience, where specific pages should be named and ordered deliberately.

visuals.name: Pie chart
visuals.useWhen: Show part-to-whole for a small number of categories, ideally five or fewer.
visuals.notFor: Beyond a handful of slices, or when close values need comparing. People compare lengths far better than angles; use barChart or treemap.

visuals.name: Matrix
visuals.useWhen: Show values across stepped row and column hierarchies, with drill-down, subtotals and aggregation.
visuals.notFor: A flat list with no hierarchy to step through. Use tableEx in that case; the extra machinery is only worth its cost when the reader will drill.

visuals.name: Python visual
visuals.exclusionReason: Needs a Python runtime; not authorable as a plain sample.
visuals.useWhen: Run a Python script as a visual, for analytics the built-in visuals cannot express.
visuals.notFor: A self-contained report. It needs a Python runtime and script execution in the consuming environment - a deployment and governance decision, not a visual one.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Needs a Python runtime, not an appearance question.

visuals.name: Q&A
visuals.exclusionReason: Q&A is not supported in PBIR authoring and is scheduled for deprecation (December 2026).
visuals.useWhen: Let a reader type a question in natural language and get a generated visual in response.
visuals.notFor: Any new work. Unsupported in PBIR authoring and scheduled for deprecation in December 2026.

visuals.name: Paginated report visual
visuals.exclusionReason: Requires a separate paginated report definition.
visuals.useWhen: Embed a paginated report for pixel-perfect, print-ready layouts.
visuals.notFor: Authoring inside this project. It requires a separate paginated report definition, which is a different artefact and a different deployment.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Needs a separate paginated report definition.

visuals.name: Real-time line chart
visuals.useWhen: A line chart that appends points as data streams in.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. Catalogued, Desktop availability unverified. Use lineChart.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Desktop availability unverified.

visuals.name: Ribbon chart
visuals.useWhen: Show which category ranks highest over time and how that ranking changes period by period.
visuals.notFor: Reading values. A ribbon encodes rank and deliberately hides magnitude, so it cannot answer 'by how much?'.

thumbnail.reason: A ribbon ranks categories and carries the second-highest value as a trailing band, which is neither a bar chart nor a stacked one. Drawn as ranked ribbons.

visuals.name: Scatter chart
visuals.useWhen: Show the relationship between two measures across many items, surfacing clusters, correlation and outliers.
visuals.notFor: A single series or a handful of points. A scatter needs density to reveal anything; use columnChart below about twenty points.

visuals.name: Goals and scorecard
visuals.exclusionReason: Catalogued, but its mapping to the current Desktop experience is unconfirmed.
visuals.useWhen: Metrics and scorecards tracking progress against business objectives, with colour-coded status.
visuals.notFor: Authoring here. `scorecard` is catalogued but its mapping to the current Desktop experience is unconfirmed.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Shares the target glyph with the KPI family; see the not-authorable reason in the catalog.

visuals.name: R visual
visuals.exclusionReason: Needs an R runtime; not authorable as a plain sample.
visuals.useWhen: Run an R script as a visual.
visuals.notFor: A self-contained report, for the same runtime reason as the Python visual.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Needs an R runtime, not an appearance question.

visuals.name: Shape
visuals.useWhen: Group or annotate a region of the canvas, or draw a line or arrow for emphasis.
visuals.notFor: Anything data-bound. A shape carries no fields.

visuals.name: Shape map
visuals.useWhen: Show a measure against custom region shapes when no standard geography fits, such as sales territories or service areas.
visuals.notFor: World geography. This is a preview feature, so confirm availability in the target Desktop build before designing around it.

visuals.name: Slicer
visuals.useWhen: Put a filter on the canvas so the reader can narrow the page without opening the Filters pane.
visuals.notFor: High-cardinality fields, where the list becomes unusable. Use a report-page filter or a search control instead.

visuals.name: Stacked area chart
visuals.useWhen: Show a cumulative total and how its composition shifts over time.
visuals.notFor: Comparing individual series rather than their sum. Only the bottom band is reliably readable against the axis.

thumbnail.reason: No distinct glyph exists for the stacked variant; the outline is identical and only the fill segmentation differs.

visuals.name: Table (legacy)
visuals.useWhen: Nothing. Present only so the gallery can explain why it is absent.
visuals.notFor: Any new work. Use tableEx.

thumbnail.reason: Legacy. Use tableEx.

visuals.name: Table
visuals.useWhen: Show exact values across many rows and columns where the reader needs the numbers themselves.
visuals.notFor: Seeing a trend. A table hides shape, so pair it with a chart rather than substituting one.

visuals.name: Text slicer
visuals.exclusionReason: Not a verified alias of the Input slicer. Do not substitute it.
visuals.useWhen: A slicer variant in the catalog.
visuals.notFor: Substituting it for the Input slicer. It is not a verified alias, and the Input slicer has no type in the catalog at all - confirm it in Desktop rather than guessing an encoding.

thumbnail.reason: Excluded type. Shares the slicer glyph. It is withheld because it is not a verified alias for the Input slicer, which is a binding question.

visuals.name: Text box
visuals.useWhen: Add a title, a caption, or a short explanation to the canvas.
visuals.notFor: Layout. Use shapes or the grid for structure - a textbox used for positioning ends up looking accidental.

visuals.name: Treemap
visuals.useWhen: Show a hierarchy as nested rectangles sized by value, where there are too many categories for a pie.
visuals.notFor: Comparing close values. Area is hard to compare precisely; use barChart when the values matter more than the structure.

visuals.name: Waterfall chart
visuals.useWhen: Explain how a starting value reaches an ending value through a series of positive and negative contributions.
visuals.notFor: Categories that are not a chain of changes. Use barChart for an unordered comparison.

visuals.name: Dual KPI
visuals.useWhen: Show two related measures against each other over a time axis, such as actual against target or this year against last year.
visuals.notFor: A single headline number - use cardVisual. The two-value structure is the point; do not bind two unrelated measures just because the roles are available.

visuals.name: Chiclet Slicer
visuals.useWhen: Filter by category using image tiles, when each category has a picture that carries meaning.
visuals.notFor: Fields without images, where it degrades to plain buttons. Use slicer or advancedSlicerVisual.

visuals.name: Tornado chart
visuals.useWhen: Contrast two measures as bars extending in opposite directions from a shared baseline, typically positive against negative variance.
visuals.notFor: Two measures that are not directly comparable - the shared baseline asserts they are. Use clusteredBarChart for an ordinary comparison.

visuals.name: Power KPI
visuals.useWhen: A designed KPI tile combining a headline value with a target and supporting detail.
visuals.notFor: A set of metrics that need comparing as a portfolio. Use Power KPI Matrix, or a pivotTable when the values are the point.

visuals.name: Gantt
visuals.useWhen: Show scheduled tasks with start date, duration, dependencies, completion and resources against a date axis.
visuals.notFor: Actual event data with irregular timestamps. A Gantt implies planned duration and sequence; use Timeline Slicer or a Gantt-shaped bar chart for events.

visuals.name: Timeline Slicer
visuals.useWhen: Brush a date range from a compact horizontal timeline.
visuals.notFor: Precise or relative date entry, which the native slicer's Between and RelativeTime modes handle directly.

visuals.name: Mekko Chart
visuals.useWhen: Carry two encodings on one mark: magnitude in bar height and share in bar width.
visuals.notFor: Many categories - both encodings become unreadable quickly. Use treemap when you want magnitude plus share in a hierarchy.

visuals.name: Sunburst
visuals.useWhen: Show a hierarchy as nested rings, with arc angle encoding value at each level.
visuals.notFor: Deep hierarchies, where inner rings get too thin to read. Use treemap - it holds more levels legibly.

visuals.name: SandDance
visuals.useWhen: Animate how a population flows through dimensions over time, so movement between states is the message.
visuals.notFor: A static report, a printed page, or a reader scanning past. It communicates by motion; if the motion is not watched it says nothing. Pair it with a still visual that carries the same finding.

visuals.name: Aster Plot
visuals.useWhen: Show how a measure is distributed within each category, exposing spread, skew and outliers rather than one aggregate per category.
visuals.notFor: Comparing category totals. That is a different question; use columnChart for the totals and aster plot for the distribution.

visuals.name: Sankey Chart
visuals.useWhen: Show directed flow between sequential stages, with link width proportional to volume.
visuals.notFor: Cycles in the data, which it cannot lay out without becoming unreadable. Model the flow acyclically or use Force-Directed Graph for a non-directional network.

visuals.name: Chord
visuals.useWhen: Show flows between two states of the same dimension, such as customers moving between tiers or between countries.
visuals.notFor: Asymmetric or one-way relationships, which it cannot represent. Use Sankey Chart when direction matters.

visuals.name: Bullet Chart
visuals.useWhen: Show actual against target against a graduated performance scale, densely enough for a row of metrics.
visuals.notFor: Trend over time. It reports status at a point, not direction; add a sparkline beside it.

visuals.name: Dot Plot
visuals.useWhen: Compare values across categories using far less ink than a bar chart, which keeps many categories readable.
visuals.notFor: Part-to-whole, and small differences that need precise reading. Use barChart when exact magnitude is the message.

visuals.name: Enhanced Scatter
visuals.useWhen: Scatter with encodings the native scatter does not offer: gradient, shape, rotation and data-bound images alongside size and colour.
visuals.notFor: Simple relationships. The native scatterChart covers Category, X, Y, Size and Legend with far less binding risk - note this visual's dataViewMappings allow only five mutually exclusive role combinations and an invalid pairing fails with 'There are too many columns'.

visuals.name: Force-Directed Graph
visuals.useWhen: Explore a network where position carries no meaning and emergent clustering is the finding.
visuals.notFor: Anything where node order matters. Layout is force-directed and not deterministic between renders, so it cannot be read as a ranking or a sequence - and its asynchronous layout means a screenshot may capture it mid-settle.

visuals.name: Infographic Designer
visuals.useWhen: Build a KPI wall of designed tiles from numbers, icons and images, where each metric is a card in its own right.
visuals.notFor: Analytical exploration. It has no fixed layout - it selects one from the fields bound to it, and an under-specified Values role is the usual reason it renders as a plain list.

visuals.name: LineDot Chart
visuals.useWhen: A line with markers plus an optional counter line, for a series where the individual points matter.
visuals.notFor: Dense series, where the markers overlap into a smear. Use lineChart when the shape matters more than the points.

visuals.name: Multi KPI
visuals.useWhen: Show several measures with status against target in a compact repeated layout.
visuals.notFor: Free-form tile layout, which Infographic Designer handles better; and very large metric sets, where a matrix reads better.

visuals.name: Power KPI Matrix
visuals.useWhen: A grid of KPI tiles, for a portfolio of metrics that need reading together.
visuals.notFor: A handful of metrics, where the grid adds chrome without adding comparison. Use a small table or a few cards.

visuals.name: Pulse Chart
visuals.useWhen: Show a current value against labelled performance bands, so the acceptable range is implied rather than explained.
visuals.notFor: Precise trend reading, and for a target that is a single fixed number rather than a range.

visuals.name: Radar Chart
visuals.useWhen: Compare a small number of entities across the same set of dimensions in one view.
visuals.notFor: More than about six dimensions or three entities. The polygon becomes spiky and area comparisons between overlapping shapes are unreliable - use a small multiple of bar charts instead.

visuals.name: Stream Graph
visuals.useWhen: Show how the composition of a total changes over time, with the shape of the mix as the message.
visuals.notFor: Reading individual series values. Bands away from the baseline have no common reference; use stackedAreaChart when the values matter.

visuals.name: Table Heatmap
visuals.useWhen: Colour table cells by value so patterns and outliers stand out across many rows and columns at once.
visuals.notFor: Precise value reading - the colour is the signal and the number becomes incidental. For both at once, use tableEx with conditional formatting, which the native visual supports.

visuals.name: Text Filter
visuals.useWhen: Free-text search across one field, for a reader who knows roughly what they want but not the exact value.
visuals.notFor: Enumerating the available values - it takes exactly one field and offers no list. Use slicer when the reader needs to see the options. Note it is a custom visual rather than a slicer in the slicer sense, despite doing a filter's job.

visuals.name: Word Cloud
visuals.useWhen: Give a rough visual sense of which terms dominate a body of unstructured text.
visuals.notFor: Accurate counts, or comparing one word against another. Area and angle are not readable quantities and font assignment is effectively arbitrary; if the reader needs to know which term is most frequent, use a bar chart of term frequency.
